Thomas Hutchins, born at Dudley in 1747, married Priscilla Dana of Pomfret, just over the Connecticut line,
in 1768. Worcester County and north-eastern Connecticut were one country of small hill farms,
and their son Cyrel was born at Pomfret in 1770; within a year they had gone north to Winchester,
New Hampshire, where his father’s family had settled.
These were the towns where the Revolution began as a farmers’ war.
When word came from Lexington on 19 April 1775, minute companies marched from towns all over the county,
and the family’s men went too. Thomas’s younger brothers Asa and Isaac, of Winchester,
served that year in Captain Jonathan Whitcomb’s company of Colonel James Reed’s New Hampshire regiment,
which held the rail fence at Bunker Hill that June.
Henry Briggs, whose granddaughter Maryette would marry Allen Dana Hutchins, enlisted in May.
And on DeWitt’s grandmother’s side, Hinsdale Hammond of Sturbridge served in Captain Abel Mason’s company in the Saratoga
campaign of 1777. The war was won in 1783, and the country to the north lay open.
